The NDP voted against the original takeover bill because it did not go far enough. This bill goes farther. At the same time, we are not opting for a public ownership solution to the extensive foreign control of the Canadian economy. We believe that a screening agency is a realistic answer to express the national interest. We also do not feel that Canadian resources should be directed toward a substantial buy-back of the foreign controlled sector. We do not believe that the future development of Canada should be jeopardized by committing our scarce funds to an enormous repatriation of the past. For instance, the book value of foreign-controlled firms exceeds $30 billion. No estimate of current market value is available. are serious economic problems in buying back foreign-owned enterprises. Let me give you an example or two. Let us look at the difficulties of buying them back. Who would buy them? Would it be government or private interests, and at what prices? How would the new owners cover the difficult transitional period from acquisition until they could operate as autonomous enterprises? It has been estimated that the loss, in real terms, due to excessive unemployment is $5 billion a year. This extra increment of production, over and above what would otherwise be the case, can be used for the elimination of poverty, elimination of slums, the construction of urban transportation systems, the provision of adequate housing, the control of pollution and the development of Canadian industries and resources by Canadians.
